title: ECharts in RO style
text: Load packages need: use small synthetic dataset throughout vignette can run everything standalone:
code: library(echarts4r) library(dplyr) # library(ROvis) library(ROvis.echarts) library(ROvis.utils) sex_levels <- c("Women", "Men", "Total")  # Reported cases per age group and sex dat_cases <- data.frame(   agegroup = rep(c("0-19", "20-39", "40-59", "60-79", "80+"), times = 3),   sex = factor(rep(sex_levels, each = 5), levels = sex_levels),   n = c(     12000,     48000,     61000,     43000,     18000,     10000,     45000,     58000,     39000,     14000,     22000,     93000,     119000,     82000,     32000   ) )  # Reported cases per week (three series) dat_weekly <- data.frame(   week = factor(rep(1:12, times = 3), levels = 1:12),   sex = factor(rep(sex_levels, each = 12), levels = sex_levels),   n = c(     800,     950,     1100,     1400,     1600,     1550,     1300,     1100,     900,     750,     600,     500,     700,     880,     1020,     1300,     1480,     1420,     1180,     990,     820,     680,     540,     440,     1500,     1830,     2120,     2700,     3080,     2970,     2480,     2090,     1720,     1430,     1140,     940   ) )

title: ECharts in RO style
text: ro_e_standard() applies RO visual style echarts4r chart adds accessibility features (see Accessibility features). slots echarts4r pipeline way ro_gg_theme() ggplot2. Add end, chart layers:
code: dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>   e_title("Cases by age group", "Women only") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_standard()

title: ECharts in RO style
text: grouped charts, group data dplyr::group_by() piping e_charts(): Use e_flip_coords() turn column chart horizontal bar chart: note x-axis variable types: x-axis variable numeric (like year week number), echarts4r treats value axis. RO theme shows grid lines value axes, end vertical grid lines well horizontal ones. avoid , make x-axis variable factor explicit levels. way echarts4r uses category axis, grid lines, order values stays correct. example, achieved : convenience, also warning displayed try :
code: dat_cases |>   group_by(sex) |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n) |>   e_title("Cases by age group and sex") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_standard(palette = "gender_con") dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>   e_flip_coords() |>   e_title("Cases by age group", "Women only") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_standard() dat_weekly |>   group_by(sex) |>   e_charts(week) |>   e_line(n) |>   e_title("Weekly cases by sex") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Week") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_standard(palette = "gender_con") # Turns week into a category axis without changing the order week = factor(rep(1:12, times = 3), levels = 1:12) data_multi <- data.frame(   year = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024),   women = c(120, 145, 160, 175, 190),   men = c(95, 110, 125, 140, 150) )  data_multi |>   e_charts(year) |>   e_bar(women, name = "Women") |>   e_bar(men, name = "Men") |>   ro_e_standard(palette = "gender_con") Warning: ! The x-axis variable is numeric, which creates a continuous axis. ℹ If not intended, convert the variable to a factor: `mutate(year =   factor(year))` tab_cases_week_by_prov <- expand.grid(   week = seq(as.Date("2022-04-01"), by = "week", length.out = 20),   Province = c("Flevoland", "Groningen", "Noord-Brabant", "Utrecht", "Zeeland") ) |>   mutate(n = sample(10:1000, n(), replace = TRUE))  tab_cases_week_by_prov |>   group_by(Province) |>   e_charts(x = week) |>   e_line(n) |>   e_axis_labels(y = "Number of cases") |>   e_x_axis(     name = "Date",     formatter = htmlwidgets::JS(       'function (value) {     var monthShortNames = ["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun",                            "Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"];     var d = new Date(value);     return monthShortNames[d.getMonth()] + "  " + d.getFullYear();   }'     )   ) |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_title("Cases per week for 5 Dutch provinces") |>   e_legend() |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "item") |>   ro_e_standard()

title: ECharts in RO style
text: default, ro_e_standard() enforces fixed aspect ratios accordance RO data visualisation guidelines: total element (title + chart + legend) 2:1 width--height, inner plot area (grid , without axis labels legend) 3:1 width--height. ratios update automatically whenever container width changes, example browser window resized Shiny sidebar toggled. controlled fixed_aspect argument, defaults TRUE. Set fixed_aspect = FALSE need control chart height , example inside Shiny app fixed-height container dashboard chart must fill exact pixel area. chart keeps height specify (via e_charts(height = …) chunk’s fig.height option) stops adjusting resize:
code: dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>   e_title("2:1 aspect ratio (default)", "fixed_aspect = TRUE") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_standard() dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   e_charts(agegroup, height = 400) |>   e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>   e_title("Fixed 400 px height (fixed_aspect = FALSE)") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_standard(fixed_aspect = FALSE)

title: ECharts in RO style
text: ro_e_standard() accepts palette argument. available palettes ones used ro_color_palette(): "categorical" (default) general categorical data "gender_con" conventional gender colors "gender_unc" unconventional gender colors "full" 18 RO colors "greys" grey tints can preview palette ro_show_colors(): Apply different palette passing name ro_e_standard():
code: ro_show_colors("categorical") ro_show_colors("gender_con") ro_show_colors("gender_unc") ro_show_colors("greys") dat_cases |>   group_by(sex) |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n) |>   e_title("Cases by age group and sex", "gender_unc palette") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_standard(palette = "gender_unc")

title: ECharts in RO style
text: Interactive charts need accessible keyboard-users. ro_e_standard() applies ro_e_theme() adds keyboard screen reader support top: Arrow keys move tooltip across data points. direction auto-detected chart orientation (left/right column line charts, /horizontal bar charts). can also set explicitly axis. chart needs focus first: Tab click . Screen readers read tooltip content every step. Tab focuses legend items; Enter Space toggles . Screen readers announce legend item button /state. legend part ro_e_theme(), also works theme alone. Screen readers announce chart title first, axes data, read axis labels axis order (left right, bottom top). needs renderer = "svg", default. Try line chart: Tab chart use arrow keys, Tab legend. ro_e_standard() takes styling arguments ro_e_theme(), plus axis: can also extend . example, case Dutch provinces: horizontal bar chart, ro_e_standard() auto-detects vertical orientation binds /arrow keys instead:
code: dat_weekly |>   group_by(sex) |>   e_charts(week) |>   e_line(n) |>   e_title(     "Weekly cases by sex",     "Use arrow keys to navigate, Tab + Enter/Space to toggle series"   ) |>   e_x_axis(name = "Week") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_standard(palette = "gender_con") tab_cases_week_by_prov |>   group_by(Province) |>   e_charts(x = week) |>   e_line(n) |>   e_axis_labels(y = "Number of cases", x = "Date") |>   e_x_axis(     formatter = htmlwidgets::JS(       'function (value) {     var monthShortNames = ["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun",                            "Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"];     var d = new Date(value);     return monthShortNames[d.getMonth()] + "  " + d.getFullYear();   }'     )   ) |>   e_title("COVID-19 cases per week for 5 Dutch provinces") |>   e_legend() |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "item") |>   ro_e_standard(axis = "both") dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>   e_flip_coords() |>   e_title("Cases by age group", "Use up/down arrow keys to navigate") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_standard()

title: ECharts in RO style
text: chart ro_e_standard() doesn’t cover, apply RO styling ro_e_theme(). takes styling arguments, adds accessibility features apart keyboard-accessible legend, prefer ro_e_standard() whenever can.
code: dat_cases |>   filter(sex == "Women") |>   e_charts(agegroup) |>   e_bar(n, name = "Women") |>   e_title("Cases by age group", "Styling only") |>   e_x_axis(name = "Age class") |>   e_y_axis(name = "Value") |>   e_tooltip(trigger = "axis") |>   ro_e_theme()
